messages:
maria: Hey @alex — customer jess reported intermittent broken pipe during streaming. They see our gateway tag the request as 5xx and they're being billed for tokens after the client abort. Repro steps below.

maria: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-v1\",\"input\":\"stream test\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true

maria: Behavior: starts streaming tokens, after ~11-13s client issues FIN, then connection dies and client shows "connection reset by peer". Our gateway records a 502 and logs contain "upstream read EPIPE".

alex: thanks — can you paste the request id + raw gateway log snippet and confirm client OS/proxy?

jess: i'm the customer here. Windows app using WinHTTP via corp proxy. Request id: req_20260310_abc123. Happens reproducibly when network flaps or user closes app. Happens ~30% of attempts.

maria: paste from gateway log:
```
{"req_id":"req_20260310_abc123","upstream_status":200,"upstream_bytes_sent":2048,"upstream_finish":"client_half_close","gateway_error":"upstream read EPIPE","billing_label":"5xx"}
```

maria: Note: upstream_status=200 and bytes_sent>0 but billing still marked as 5xx.

sachin: I captured pcap. Sequence is: server sends final chunk(s) and flushes, client issues FIN, proxy replies with RST ~120ms later. Our edge interprets RST as upstream failure when it arrives after the socket half-close. Essentially we treat post-data RST as upstream crash.

alex: ok — two angles: telemetry and heuristic. Telemetry: add tag `observed_client_abort_after_data` so we can count. Heuristic: only mark 5xx if no bytes were sent or if upstream_status is actually a 5xx. Right now code marks 5xx for any connErr after stream.

sachin: quick patch idea — require both `connErr` and `bytesSent==0` OR `upstreamStatus>=500` to mark 5xx. Small diff: 
```diff
- if connErr && bytesSent==0 { mark5xx() }
+ if connErr && bytesSent==0 && upstreamStatus<500 { // keep previous behavior }
+ if connErr && (bytesSent==0 || upstreamStatus>=500) { mark5xx() }
```
(we'll make it cleaner in main branch)

alex: also add explicit check for chunked-encoding trailer finalize. If we saw a proper chunked end ("0\r\n\r\n") before FIN, treat as successful. That avoids classifying network-proxy RSTs that happen after well-formed stream end.

maria: Customer is worried about billing. Can we ship a toggle to opt the customer out of strict EOF heuristic until the fix rolls?

sachin: yes — add a runtime flag `streaming.strict_eof=true` default. For this tenant set false; gateway will not retroactively mark 5xx for post-data aborts and we will trigger refund workflow. Patch in review.

alex: test plan: emulate WinHTTP by sending: server sends some event-stream lines, then half-close (FIN) from client, then RST from proxy after 100ms. Verify gateway does not label 5xx if bytes_sent>0 or chunked end seen. Add unit + e2e.

maria: Shipping plan? Can we get a staged deploy to hosted customers and flag the tenant?

ops-bot: deploy scheduled — gateway v1.72.4 -> canary at 2026-03-11T02:00Z, prod rollout 2026-03-11T06:00Z.

maria: Customer updated: we reproduced, created tenant toggle, and will refund the overbilled invoice. jess: please confirm after deploy.

jess: confirmed after patch and toggle, no further billing and streaming behaves. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
notes: managed refund and created toggle; patch created; scheduled deploy
